Evan — follow-up from the demo prep. I captured the core capabilities we'll include in the questionnaire. I'm pasting concise answers here so you have them immediately; the formal sheet + artifacts are attached.

SCIM provisioning
- Protocol: SCIM 2.0 (RFC7643, RFC7644) supported.
- Bulk operations: we support PATCH and bulk replace semantics for groups and users via batched requests; for very large tenants we recommend our async bulk endpoint (see attachment).
- Filtering & scoping: supports SCIM filter expressions. You can limit sync to groups by attribute (e.g., dept eq "payments"). We also support group-to-role mapping rules in the Redwood console.
- Latency & rate limits: default provisioning rate is 10 reqs/sec per tenant; burstable to 50 reqs/sec for Dedicated customers. Average perceived provisioning latency is under 8s for single-user create; groups (size < 5k) typically sync within 90s in normal load. We include webhook feedback for job completion.
- Deprovisioning: soft-delete + configurable retention window; immediate disabled flag support with option to fully remove on policy.

SSO (SAML / OIDC)
- SAML: SP-initiated and IdP-initiated supported; SAML 2.0 with SP metadata export and assertion consumer endpoints. Supports signed assertions and encrypted attributes.
- OIDC: supports standard OIDC flows including Authorization Code + PKCE, and token introspection endpoints for session validation.
- Attribute mapping: flexible attribute transform rules; we provide prebuilt mappings for common IdPs (Okta, Azure AD, Ping).
- Session & token revocation: admin-triggered session invalidation and OAuth token revocation endpoints available; access tokens are short-lived (default 15m), refresh tokens rotation supported.

RBAC & admin controls
- Roles: hierarchical role model — platform roles (org admin, billing), product roles (service admin), and resource-scoped roles (project-level).
- Custom roles: yes — create roles with fine-grained permissions and JSON rule export/import.
- Delegated admin: can create tenant-level delegated admins with scoped permissions and MFA enforcement.
- Approval workflows: optional approval flows for privilege escalation (can be wired to IdP or external ticketing).

Audit & evidence
- Audit logs: immutable event stream for user lifecycle, admin actions, and token events. Retention: default 1 year; enterprise plans can configure up to 7 years. Logs are exportable to S3, Datadog, or SIEM via streaming.
- Evidence artifacts: screenshots, role-mapping export, SCIM schema sample, and a short playbook showing admin onboarding.

Next steps: I'll attach redwood_scim_schema_sample.json and a short role-mapping-playbook.pdf. If you need a sample SCIM filter for group->role mapping, say which attribute you want to drive mapping (e.g., group.displayName or custom attribute).

Evan — attached is our completed questionnaire (ApexTrust_IAM_Questionnaire_v1.xlsx), the SCIM schema sample (redwood_scim_schema_sample.json) and a short role-mapping playbook. Below are direct answers to your security follow-ups so they are easy to find: 

1) SCIM server-side filtering: yes. Redwood supports server-side filtering and incremental delta syncs. We accept push deltas from IdPs and will apply pre-configured filter rules on receipt (e.g., department eq "payments" or custom attribute filtering). For very large group catalogs we recommend our async bulk endpoint to avoid listing operations — we included an example call in the schema sample.

2) Refresh token rotation & compromise handling: default refresh TTL is 30 days; maximum configurable up to 365 days for enterprise plans. We strongly recommend refresh token rotation (we enable rotation by default) — when rotation detects reuse we revoke the existing session and issue an admin alert. Revocation endpoints support immediate invalidation and an admin can escalate to tenant-wide forced logout.

3) Audit retention & encryption: enterprise customers can configure audit retention up to 7 years. Logs are tamper-evident (append-only stores with HMAC checks) and can be encrypted using customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM integration). We provide S3 exports with server-side encryption or direct streaming into your SIEM via TLS with mutual auth.

Attachments contain sample API calls and a short runbook for onboarding a delegated admin. If you want any adjustments to retention or TTL defaults we can include them in the contract appendix.
